correctness.rationale: The positive moment operator is trace class for every fixed small dilation. Near its rank-one limit, analytic perturbation gives top eigenvector e0+eps*m*e1+eps^2*(q*e2-m^2*e0/2)+O(eps^3). Its second spectral value is O(eps^2) by the positive compression bound. Kernels can be restricted to real nonnegative parameters by matrix-entry positivity; compactness gives an interior optimizer. Comparison with the kernel at eps*m forces the optimizer to differ from eps*m by O(eps^2); the squared transversal mismatch is eps^4*((q-m^2)^2+b^2)+o(eps^4). The spectral gap turns this into a norm deficit with factor 1/2, whose minimum is achieved at b=0. The zero-variance point-mass case has exact equality. Finite verification: 20 checks across two measures and three scales; no use of finite tests as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The quantity is the natural quantitative failure of kernel-norm testing at the rank-one boundary in the positive moment-Hankel cone, where exact attainment is already qualitatively understood. The unexpected universality is that every compactly supported positive measure has the same fourth-order defect law depending only on squared variance, despite arbitrary higher moments; two-atom and continuous examples have sharp different constants. This local structural stability invariant gives substantially more information than a qualitative failure of SRKT.
